title: Exponential smoothing and an overview of ARIMA and Prophet

videos.script: To forecast next week, the simplest idea is to repeat last week. The next simplest is to average every week you have. {{two}} Both are wrong in an instructive way. The first trusts one noisy week completely. The second trusts a week from three years ago as much as yesterday. {{wrong}} Exponential smoothing sits between them. Recent weeks count most, and each older week counts a little less than the one after it. {{weights}} One number decides how fast the memory fades. {{alpha}} Add a trend and a season to that idea and you have Holt-Winters, which has forecast retail sales since the nineteen-sixties. {{hw}} ARIMA comes from a different idea: describe how each week depends on the weeks before it, and on the errors made forecasting them. {{arima}} And Prophet, a library from Facebook, fits a trend with bends in it, seasons, and holidays you list for it. {{prophet}} This lesson fits the first two to Panela's weeks, and explains the third. Then it asks the question that matters most: better than what? {{end}}
